# dsh-quick-screenshot
English | 中文

One-click screenshots of the DeepSeek Harness window, placed straight into the
composer draft.

It is one self-contained DSH bundle: a Host half that captures the DSH window (or
a window / the who

le desktop) through the platform's own tooling and serves the
PNG over one authenticated Fetch route

, and a hand-written Client half served as
the package's `./client` bundle.
## What it adds
| Seat | Result |
| `shell.overlay` | A **floating camera control** over the whole window, so a screenshot works on ev
ery page — not only where a composer happens to be mounted. Drag it anywhere; the anchor persists in

`localStorage`. |
| `conversation.input.left` | The same control in the composer's left tool row, n

ge`. |
| `conversation.input.left` | The same control in the composer's left tool row, next to `+` |
| Gesture | Capture target |
| Click | The DeepSeek Harness window (largest visible window whose title contains `DeepSeek Harness

`, falling back to the foreground window) |
| Shift+click | The whole desktop, every monitor |
| Alt

+click | Whatever window is currently in the foreground |
| `Ctrl+Shift+S` | The same as a plain cli
ck, from anywhere on the page |

Where the image lands depends on what is on screen: a mounted composer's draft
takes it as an attach

ment, so the next message carries the image; with no
composer mounted the PNG goes to the clipboard,

ready to paste into the
conversation the reader navigates to. A click never steals the keyboard —
`
mousedown` is prevented, so the caret stays where it was.

The control reports what happened in place: a spinner while the Host captures,
`已放入输入框` with the cap

tured pixel size for a few seconds afterwards, or the
Host's own refusal text when the capture faile

d. The tooltip carries the full
gesture list and the last result.
## Where the image goes

With a composer mounted, the Client half follows the path the composer's own
paste and drop intake t

a composer mounted, the Client half follows the path the composer's own
paste and drop intake take:

1. `POST /api/quick-screenshot` returns the PNG bytes (and a small metadata header).
2. `ctx.convers

ation.createDrafts(sessionId, [file])` registers the browser file
and returns its draft id.
3. The `

inputActions` standard prop admits those ids with
`addAttachments(ids)` — the composer's rail then s

hows the thumbnail and the
send serializes the image with the message.

With no composer mounted (the plugins page, Trajectory, Settings …) the same
capture is written to t

he system clipboard instead, and the result bubble says
so — paste it into a composer when the reade

r gets there. If the clipboard
refuses the write, the bubble names the staged PNG on disk instead.

When those services are unavailable, the client falls back to dispatching a
synthetic `paste` event

carrying the file on `[data-composer-input="true"]`,
which is exactly what a manual paste does.
## Host route

`GET /api/quick-screenshot` describes what this Host can capture right now
(`supported`, `platform`,

`tool`, `modes`, `directory`); `POST /api/quick-screenshot`
takes an optional JSON body and answers

s`, `directory`); `POST /api/quick-screenshot`
takes an optional JSON body and answers with the PNG:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Field | Meaning |

| `mode` | `window` (default), `active`, or `screen` |
| `titlePattern` | Window title matched by `w

indow` mode; defaults to `DeepSeek Harness` |
| `maxDimension` | Optional cap on the longest side; `
0` keeps the native capture size |

The response is `image/png` with `Cache-Control: no-store` and one
`X-Screenshot` header carrying pe

rcent-encoded JSON metadata
(`mode`, `method`, `window`, `width`, `height`, `bytes`, `path`). Failur

es answer JSON
with a stable `code` (`CAPTURE_UNSUPPORTED`, `CAPTURE_TIMEOUT`, `CAPTURE_FAILED`,
`ME

THOD_NOT_ALLOWED`) and a message meant for the user. Both methods are
registered through `ctx.connec

tion.fetch`, so the shared `/api` bridge applies
Host/Origin validation and browser-cookie authentic
ation before the handler runs.
## Capture backends
| Platform | Tool | Notes |
| Windows | `powershell.exe` + `System.Drawing` | `PrintWindow(PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT)` first, so an o
ccluded window still captures; a flat result falls back to reading the same rectangle off the screen

after raising the window. Per-monitor-v2 DPI aware. |
| macOS | `screencapture -x -o` | Display cap

ture; `window`/`active` both resolve to the active display. |
| Linux | first of `gnome-screenshot`,
`spectacle`, `grim`, `import`, `scrot` | Display capture. |

`DSH_SCREENSHOT_POWERSHELL` overrides the Windows shell (useful when only
PowerShell 7 is installed)

DSH_SCREENSHOT_POWERSHELL` overrides the Windows shell (useful when only
PowerShell 7 is installed).

Captures are staged in `<tmpdir>/dsh-screenshot/`, and the directory keeps only
its newest 24 files,

so the plugin owns no durable state and never grows
unbounded. One capture at a time: concurrent cl
icks queue instead of racing.
## Install

Run the DSH Plugin Manager's `install_bundle` against this directory (a local
path spec), or add it

to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` after installing it
[该节后续省略]
## Known limitations

- **Window capture excludes overlapping windows but not popups.** `PrintWindow`
renders the window's

own content; an open context menu drawn in a separate
popup window is not part of it.
- **The scree

n rectangle fallback needs the window on top.** It is only used when
`PrintWindow` returns a flat im

age, and it raises the target window first.
- **macOS and Linux capture the display**, not one chose

n window.
- **Images need an image-capable model.** A text-only model refuses the
attachment at send

time with the composer's own error banner.
- **The chord is a web chord.** A browser that reserves

`Ctrl+Shift+S` (Save as)
absorbs it before the page sees it; the button always works.
- **The Electr

on desktop shell is served over `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`**, so the
Client half reaches `/api/quick-
screenshot` as a same-origin request there as well.
